title: Client pin + slow priming cheatsheet
content:
Purpose: quick reference for a client-targeted version pin + slow priming approach. Goal is to reduce cold-KV and cold-cache regressions when flipping clients to a new model variant without large instant traffic shifts.

Context / motivation:
- We've seen two classes of issues on model flips: (A) immediate quality regressions due to model diffs, (B) throughput/latency spikes from cold KV cache and tokenization/allocator warmup.
- For high-value clients we want deterministic, low-risk flips: pin client -> prime KV/cache -> ramp traffic -> validate metrics -> promote.

Core idea: pin-and-slow-prime
1) Pin client routing to target model variant (route still at 0% traffic externally) so requests from client go to the variant and populate its caches, but we keep outward traffic fraction low.
2) Use a steady priming cadence (short warmup requests) to seed per-tenant KV/cache ahead of user spikes.
3) Ramp fraction in tiny steps with telemetry gates.

Priming recipe (practical):
- Priming window: 30–120 minutes depending on expected session length.
- Priming traffic: 1–5 QPS of synthetic warmup requests per client (or 0.1x baseline if production flows are available).
- Warmup prompts: 12–20 short requests that mirror real user prefixes (short + medium contexts). Keep token length distribution similar to client historical.
- Sequence: send prompt set once, pause 2–5 min, repeat x3. Goal = populate KV cache & LRU buffers.
- For chat-style clients, include last-turns-history-like prompts to exercise attention cache.

Cohort sizing & schedule:
- Micro-cohort (safest): 1–3 clients, warm for 60–90m, then 1% traffic ramp every 30m.
- Small cohort: 5–10 clients, warm 30–60m, 2% every 30m.
- Large cohort: >10 clients used only after successful micro cohorts.

Traffic ramping heuristics (gates):
- Per-minute error rate (5xx) <= baseline + 0.5% absolute
- P99 latency <= baseline * 1.25 (or +150ms cap)
- Token generation quality checks: perplexity spike or eval prompt delta <= predefined threshold
- Cost/throughput: GPU util < 85% (dedicated), queue length stable
- Telemetry: event-level sampling to check output diffs (small eval set per client)

Rollback / escape hatches:
- Immediate unpin (route client back to stable variant) if any one of:
  - 5xx > baseline + 2% absolute for 3 consecutive minutes
  - P99 latency > baseline * 1.5 for 10m
  - Manual ops abort (Pager/Slack escalation)
- Fast pinback: revert routing rule, schedule quick KV flush for failed variant to avoid sticky bad states.

Observability checklist (must have before ramping):
- Per-client per-variant time series: request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, GPU util (if dedicated)
- Small eval harness: 20 test prompts with golden answers; daily BLEU/ROUGE-like diffs or human-annotated QC if available
- Token-level cost delta (expected vs observed)
- Sampled traces with KV hit/miss breakdown and runtime kernel fallbacks
- Log lines to link requests to client pin id and warmup session id

Operational playbook (step-by-step):
1) Prepare rollout: pick client(s), create routing rule (pin) in console with metadata tag 'pin-prime-<client>-<date>'
2) Create priming job: in console -> devops -> 'priming jobs' -> upload warmup prompt set (label with client tag). Use schedule: immediate x3 cycles
3) Start priming: kick off job, watch KV hit ratio and p95 latency for variant (expect slight increase during priming but should stabilize)
4) Post-prime QA: run eval harness against sampled outputs; ping client success contact if necessary
5) Ramp traffic fractions slowly using route weights: 0.1% -> 0.5% -> 1% -> ... with 30m–1h observation windows
6) If gates pass at each step, continue. If fail, execute rollback immediately and annotate change in release doc.

Quick checklist (copyable):
- [ ] Create pin routing rule with tag
- [ ] Upload warmup prompt set (12–20 prompts)
- [ ] Start priming job (3 cycles)
- [ ] Enable per-client eval harness sampling
- [ ] Monitor gates 30m after each ramp step
- [ ] Document results + screenshots in ticket

Test prompts hints:
- Prefer short, often-seen prefixes + realistic punctuation/noise
- Include edge cases for the client product (e.g., code snippets, markup, bullet lists)
- Mix completion-lengths to exercise KV cache and attention states

Open questions / tradeoffs (things to decide per rollout):
- How aggressive should priming be when client SLAs require low added traffic? (tradeoff: longer priming vs risk of cold failures)
- Should we rely on synthetic prompts or use a scrubbed replay of real user prefixes? (privacy + replay risk)
- How to coordinate with Dedicated pool autoscaler (priming might push util above scale thresholds)

Notes to self / ops tips:
- Tag every routing rule with the ticket/JIRA id; makes postmortem auditing trivial.
- Keep one small 'canary-client' account for rehearsal runs.
- If KV warmup is the main cost, consider a targeted prefix-cache API call (work with runtime team to expose lightweight priming endpoint).
- For clients behind mobile SDKs, expect session-churn; prefer slightly longer priming windows.

Record of last run (scratch):
- 2025-01-28: client 'acme-intent' primed -> micro cohort (1 client). Priming 45m, 15 warm prompts x3. Observed: KV hit up from 12% -> 78%, p95 latency +40ms then stabilized. No quality alerts. Next: 1% traffic ramp scheduled 2025-02-03.
